# RL Training Run Diagnosis: Search-R1 / Qwen2.5-3B (GRPO)

## Verdict

**Unhealthy.** The held-out metric (`eval/nq_test`, Natural-Questions exact-match accuracy)
plateaus early and the policy collapses to a degenerate, search-free short-answer mode.
The run is not a crash and contains no instability, but it has stalled: after a short
early rise, held-out EM flattens for ~130 steps while response length collapses to ~10
tokens and the RL gradient signal vanishes.

## Held-out evidence (the arbiter)

`eval/nq_test` across the 200-step window (eval interval 10, held-out nq_test split):

| step | EM | eval resp len | eval trunc ratio |
|-----:|------:|------:|------:|
| 0  | 0.048 | 1568.6 | 0.381 |
| 29 | 0.105 | 78.9  | 0.013 |
| 49 | 0.131 | 25.0  | 0.002 |
| 69 | 0.159 | 14.4  | 0.0003 |
| 99 | 0.154 | 15.1  | 0.0007 |
| 139| 0.162 | 10.3  | 0.0 |
| 199| 0.165 | 9.8   | 0.0 |

EM rises 0.048 -> 0.159 over steps 0-69, then moves only 0.159 -> 0.165 over the remaining
130 steps. The held-out curve is flat after step 69. Training reward climbing is not
sufficient: the held-out metric, which is what the task fixes, stopped improving.

The collapse is visible in the same held-out trace: eval response length falls from 1568
(step 0) to ~10 tokens (step 199). A ~10-token completion is too short to contain a
`<think>...<search>...<information>...<answer>` trajectory. On a retrieval-augmented QA
task, the policy has stopped calling the search tool at evaluation time. That is the
failure mode the held-out data exposes.

## Root cause 1: the reward is effectively binary; the format-shaping term is dead code

`generate_with_search.reward_func` calls `compute_score_em(..., format_score=0.2)` from
`SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["format_score"]`. But in `qa_em_format.py::compute_score_em` the
`format_score` parameter is never read. The body uses `structure_format_score`,
`retrieval_score`, and `final_format_score`, all of which default to 0 and are not set
by the caller. The inline comments (`# 0.2`, `# 0.3`, `# 0.8`, `# 0.1`) describe the
intended shaped reward, but none of those values are wired in. Effective reward:

- exact-match answer present -> 1.0 (regardless of format)
- anything else -> 0.0

There is no partial credit for valid format, no credit for correct retrieval, and no
penalty shaping. This is a sparse, binary reward.

Connection to observed behavior: under GRPO with `n_samples_per_prompt=8` and
`rewards_normalization=true`, a prompt group produces a non-zero advantage only when its
8 samples disagree in reward. With a binary reward on a hard EM task, most groups are
all-wrong (reward 0 for all 8) or, less often, all-correct -> zero within-group reward
standard deviation -> zero advantage -> zero gradient. The log confirms this directly:
`rollout/zero_std/count_0` averages ~11.5 of 32 prompts (and rises to 25-30 late), and
the per-rollout `rollout/advantages` and `rollout/rewards` are ~1e-9 (floating-point
noise) for every logged step. `rollout/kl` is 0.0 throughout. The policy is receiving
essentially no learning signal, which is exactly why EM stops climbing after the early
collapse phase.

## Root cause 2: no exploration pressure enables mode collapse to short answers

`entropy_coef=0.0` (config and `run_qwen2.5_3B.sh`), so there is no entropy bonus
counteracting collapse. Combined with the binary reward above and `eps_clip=0.2 /
eps_clip_high=0.28`, the configuration is the standard recipe for mode collapse: a
policy under a sparse 0/1 reward with no exploration term and tiny advantages will
drift toward whatever mode first scores, then stay there.

The observed collapse: training `rollout/response_len/mean` goes 1751 (step 0) -> 962
(step 10) -> 197 (step 20) -> 41 (step 30) -> 10.5 (step 50) and then sits at ~9-12 for
the remaining 150 steps. The eval-length curve matches it. The early EM rise (0.048 ->
0.159) coincides with this length drop, because the base model's initial 1750-token
ramblings were hitting the 1024 response cap (train truncation 0.406 at step 0) and
scoring 0; shedding that rambling incidentally raised EM. But the policy overshot:
it abandoned multi-turn search-then-answer entirely and emits a ~10-token direct
answer, which caps EM at ~0.16 because the model no longer retrieves evidence.

This is reward hacking via mode collapse, not a healthy fix. The model traded
rambling for answer-only shortcuts, and the sparse reward gave it no signal to recover
the search behavior.

## Symptoms (not root causes)

- **Truncation ratio -> 0.** Train truncation falls 0.406 -> 0 by step 40 and stays
  there; eval follows. This is a *consequence* of responses shrinking to ~10 tokens
  (short outputs no longer hit the 1024 cap), not a defect in its own right. A
  truncated log is not proof of a defect, and here the vanishing truncation is the
  shadow of the length collapse, not its cause.
- **Held-out EM plateau at ~0.16.** Consequence of (1) no gradient from the binary
  reward and (2) the policy having collapsed away from retrieval.
- **`rollout/advantages`/`rollout/rewards` ~1e-9 and `kl` = 0.0.** Consequence of the
  zero-std groups from the binary reward and the resulting near-zero parameter
  movement. `use_kl_loss=true` with `kl_loss_coef=0.001` is set, but KL stays 0 because
  the policy barely moves.
- **`rollout/raw_reward` rising (0.039 -> 0.27).** This is the pre-normalization
  reward. It rises because the collapse made more rollouts hit exact-match, but after
  GRPO group normalization the usable reward is ~1e-9. Training reward alone does not
  establish held-out health.

## Causal chain

Binary reward (dead `format_score` shaping) -> most 8-sample groups have identical
rewards -> zero advantage / zero gradient (advantages ~1e-9, zero_std groups ~11-25 of
32). No entropy bonus (`entropy_coef=0.0`) and no shaping reward leave nothing to
prevent collapse -> policy collapses to ~10-token, search-free answers (resp len
1751 -> ~10, truncation -> 0). Early EM rises as rambling is shed, then plateaus at
~0.16 for 130 steps because the model has abandoned retrieval and there is no gradient
to recover it. Held-out EM stagnation is the downstream evidence that the run is
unhealthy, independent of the training reward.

## Notes on what was checked and not found

- No NaN/inf or optimizer instability; `check_for_nan_in_loss_and_grad=true` is set and
  no NaN appears in the trace. `run_once` receipt is `ok`, `returncode 0`.
- The `cybertron-751761.log` and its `.stderr.log` contain only Teleport session-upload
  S3 403 errors from a logging side-channel; they are unrelated to training and are not
  the cause of the plateau.
- The manifest/metrics "attempt" field disagrees (3 vs 1) and two wandb run dirs are
  listed (a restart), but these are bookkeeping; the frozen 200-step window is
  internally consistent across `eval_scores.json`, `metrics.json`, and the wandb
  `output.log`.
- The dataset, held-out set, model, 200-step budget, and eval interval are fixed per
  the task and were not modified. No fix is proposed.

# Diagnosis: GRPO / Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct / TACO run (outputs/2026-09-26/10-48-56, wandb l7my3znq)

## Verdict: UNHEALTHY — the policy never learns; the run is defective, not merely slow or noisy.

## Root cause: transposed advantage broadcast in `compute_grpo_outcome_advantage`

`verl/trainer/ppo/core_algos.py`, lines 329–335 (the estimator selected by `algorithm.adv_estimator=grpo`, called directly from `ray_trainer.compute_advantage`, lines 235–247):

```python
seq_len = response_mask.size(1)
row = scores.reshape(1, -1)                       # (1, bsz): per-sample advantages laid along the TOKEN axis
if row.size(1) < seq_len:
    row = torch.nn.functional.pad(row, (0, seq_len - row.size(1)))
else:
    row = row[:, :seq_len]
scores = row.expand(response_mask.size(0), -1) * response_mask   # same row copied to EVERY sample
```

Every other estimator in the same file broadcasts the per-sample scalar across tokens (`scores.unsqueeze(-1) * response_mask`, lines 363/535/640/694/832/870). The GRPO path instead puts the 128 group-normalized advantages (16 prompts × n=8) into one row indexed by *token position*, zero-pads it to `response_length=4096`, and copies it to every sequence. Consequently, for every sample `i` and token `t`: `A[i,t] = adv_of_sample_t` for `t<128`, and `A[i,t] = 0` for `t≥128`. The advantage a token receives has no relationship to the reward of the sequence it belongs to, and tokens past position 127 (most tokens, mean response length 170–450) receive no gradient at all.

The actor consumes this tensor unchanged (`verl/workers/utils/losses.py` line 96 → `compute_policy_loss_vanilla`, `pg_losses1 = -advantages * ratio`, token-mean aggregation). The reward function itself works and the group structure is intact: `critic/rewards/max = 1` on all 280 logged steps (no step without a fully-passing sample), `critic/advantages/max ≈ 2.47` / `min ≈ −2.47`, which are exactly the GRPO values for 1-of-8 / 7-of-8 groups. The learning signal exists at the sample level and is destroyed only at the broadcast.

## Evidence that this code path is what ran, and that it is causal (not just unusual)

1. **Exact-zero policy loss whenever no response is shorter than 128 tokens.** With the transposed row, a sequence of length ≥128 sums all 128 normalized advantages, which are zero by construction, so its token-mean advantage is identically 0. The only two steps where `response_length/min ≥ 128` (step 241: min 150, reward mean 0.219, adv range ±2.47; step 242: min 135, reward mean 0.0625, adv range [−1.62, 2.47]) have `actor/pg_loss = 4.0e-10` and `0.0`, `critic/advantages/mean = −6e-10` / `9e-10`, while `grad_norm` is non-zero (0.24, 0.16). Under a correct per-sample broadcast the token-mean advantage is a length-weighted mean of ±2.47/−0.35 values and cannot cancel to 1e-10. (Steps 18/132/209 also show pg_loss = 0, but there `advantages/max = min = 0` and `grad_norm = 0`, i.e. a legitimately degenerate batch — distinguishable from 241/242.)
2. **|pg_loss| is governed by how many responses are shorter than 128 tokens, not by reward.** Bucketing steps by `response_length/min`: <32 → median |pg_loss| 1.3e-3 (n=117); <64 → 3.9e-4 (n=124); <128 → 1.1e-4 (n=37); ≥128 → 2e-10 (n=2). Windowed |advantages/mean| falls from 1.8e-3 (steps 1–20, mean length 174) to ~1e-5 (steps 205–284, mean length ~440), correlation(|pg_loss|, mean response length) = −0.60. This is the signature of the padded row (`A[i,t]=0` for `t≥128`, partial sums only from short responses) and has no explanation under the intended algorithm.
3. **`pg_loss == −critic/advantages/mean` to ~1e-9 on every step**, confirming the actor uses exactly this advantage tensor with ratio ≡ 1 (strictly on-policy: train_batch 16 == ppo_mini_batch 16, ppo_epochs 1; `pg_clipfrac = ppo_kl = 0` on every step is therefore expected, not a defect).

## Observed outcome (symptoms, in causal order)

- **Held-out evidence (184 TACO problems, val every 50 steps, T=0.7, n=1):** `val-core/taco/acc/mean@1` = 0.0761 (step 0) → 0.0489 → 0.0598 → 0.0707 → 0.0435 → 0.0543 (step 250); `val-aux/taco/pass_rate/mean@1` = 0.195 → 0.201 → 0.216 → 0.226 → 0.177 → 0.195. All points are within ±1.5 SE (≈0.018) of the untrained baseline; the final value is below it. No held-out improvement after 250 steps.
- **Training reward is flat:** `critic/rewards/mean` per 50-step block = 0.119, 0.129, 0.128, 0.131, 0.120, 0.094 (steps 1–284); first-20 mean 0.125 vs last-20 mean 0.096. Rewards never trend up although the optimizer is updating (grad_norm 0.17–0.38, clip_grad 1.0, lr 1e-6 constant).
- **Reward-decorrelated drift:** actor entropy rises 0.47 → 0.56–0.60 and mean response length grows 174 → ~440 tokens while reward does not move; grad_norm decays 0.38 → 0.18. The updates push per-position token likelihoods with signs unrelated to outcome, so the model random-walks rather than converges.

## Things checked and ruled out as causes

- **Rollout/trainer consistency:** `rollout_corr/kl ≈ 5–8e-4`, `training/rollout_actor_probs_pearson_corr = 0.9995`, `rollout_probs_diff_mean ≈ 0.004` — vLLM 0.17 async rollout and FSDP actor agree; no stale-weight or dtype mismatch.
- **Truncation:** `response_length/clip_ratio` is 0 on most steps and never exceeds 1/128 (at most one capped sample per step; 20-step window means ≤ 0.0004); prompt max 1908 < 2048 (`filter_overlong_prompts=True`, `truncation=error` never triggered). No truncation-driven reward loss.
- **Data/reward plumbing:** train (8368) and test (184) parquet share schema, prompt template, `code_type`/`fn_name` consistency and `n_tests == len(inputs)`; `NaiveRewardManager.run_single` passes `solution_str`/`ground_truth`/`extra_info` to `taco.py:compute_score`, scores land on the last valid response token, GRPO groups by `uid`. Binary all-tests-pass reward is sparse (test problems average 204 tests, train median 5; some samples hit the 120 s `global_timeout`, `timing_s/agent_loop/compute_score/max ≈ 121 s`), which makes evaluation slow and conservative, but 277 of 280 logged steps contain at least one mixed group (`critic/advantages/max > 0`; only steps 18/132/209 are all-zero), so the sparse reward is not what prevents learning.
- **Optimizer settings:** lr 1e-6 constant, no KL/entropy terms, token-mean loss, 4×A800 instead of the script's 8 GPUs (hydra override `n_gpus_per_node=4`) — all change throughput/scale only; none can make the gradient uncorrelated with reward.
- **Log truncation:** `output.log` ends at step 284/400 (checkpoint-free run, `save_freq=400`). This limits the budget consumed but is not itself a defect; the six held-out evaluations already span 250 steps with no learning.

## Summary of root cause vs. symptoms

- Root cause: `compute_grpo_outcome_advantage` (core_algos.py 329–335) broadcasts the batch vector of advantages along the token axis instead of the batch axis, assigning sample-`t`'s advantage to token position `t` of every sequence and zero to positions ≥128.
- Direct consequences: policy gradient uncorrelated with sequence reward; roughly 59% of generated tokens over the run (≈69% after step 150, mean length ≥ 325) sit at positions ≥128 and get zero gradient; `pg_loss`/`advantages/mean` collapse exactly to 0 whenever all responses exceed 128 tokens.
- Symptoms: flat/declining held-out acc (0.076 → 0.054) and pass_rate, flat training reward (~0.12 → 0.09), rising entropy and response length, decaying grad_norm, despite healthy rollout–trainer agreement, no truncation, and a functioning reward.

# Verdict: UNHEALTHY

The GRPO training run for Search-R1 (retrieval-augmented Q&A on Qwen2.5-3B) is unhealthy. Held-out evaluation (`eval/nq_test`, Natural Questions exact-match over the first 3000 test rows) rises from 0.048 (step 0) to ~0.165 (step ~69) and then **flatlines at ~0.15–0.165 through step 199** — 130+ steps with no meaningful gain. At the same time the model **collapses to degenerate, terse direct answers**: eval response length falls from 1569 → ~9.8 tokens and truncation 0.381 → 0; rollout response length falls 1751 → ~10 tokens and truncation 0.406 → 0. Training reward alone (raw_reward ~3–27%) does not establish held-out health, and here it actually rises slightly as the model collapses — the model is learning a shortcut, not the search-reasoning task.

## Root cause

The reward signal is effectively a **binary exact-match (EM) label, with all intended shape/partial-credit dead**, and a **broken format validator**. This gives GRPO no gradient signal for the search/retrieval/reasoning behavior the recipe is meant to teach.

1. **Dead reward-shaping parameter.** `examples/search-r1/generate_with_search.py:277-293` calls
   `compute_score_em(..., format_score=SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["format_score"])` with `format_score=0.2`
   (config at `generate_with_search.py:37`). But in `examples/search-r1/qa_em_format.py:156-208`,
   `compute_score_em`'s body **never references `format_score`**. Its only shaping terms are
   `structure_format_score`, `final_format_score`, and `retrieval_score`, all defaulting to `0`.
   Every return branch therefore evaluates to one of `0`, `score` (1.0), or `score - structure_format_score` (1.0 − 0 = 1.0).
   The partial-credit ladder the comments advertise (`# 0.2`, `# 0.3`, `# 0.8`, `# 0.1`) is dead code — the reward is exactly `{0, 1}`.

2. **The format validator is itself broken, compounding (1).** `is_valid_sequence` (`qa_em_format.py:51-123`)
   splits on angle-bracket tags via `re.split(r"(</?(?:think|search|information|answer)>)", ...)` (line 74),
   but its state machine then compares the resulting parts against the space-prefixed strings
   `" thinking"` (line 89) and `" response"` (line 91), which the split regex never produces (it splits on
   `<...>` tags, not the ` thinking`/` response` tokens the Search-R1 template actually emits; verified by
   tracing the split output — the parts are `' thinking'`, `'<search>'`, etc., none of which match `" thinking"`).
   `is_valid_sequence` therefore returns False for the real trajectory format, which is what keeps the
   correct-answer branch on the `score - structure_format_score` = 1.0 path and suppresses the retrieval/format
   bonuses — the practical effect of the dead shaping in (1).

## Causal chain (evidence)

- Group-normalized GRPO with **binary** reward yields near-zero advantages. The run uses `n-samples-per-prompt 8` and per-group mean/std normalization (config.yaml). Most of the 8 samples score 0, so the group std is tiny or zero: `rollout/rewards` sits at ~1e-9 throughout, and `rollout/zero_std/count_0` shows **17–27 of the 32 groups per step with zero reward variance** — i.e. over half of the batch contributes no learning signal.
- With no reward for format, retrieval, or partial reasoning, the search scaffolding is pure token-cost with no payoff. The optimizer finds the cheapest path to EM: **emit a minimal direct answer and skip search entirely**. `rollout/response_lengths` collapses 1751 → ~10 tokens by rollout ~50 and `rollout/truncated` drops 0.406 → 0.
- Because the format validator is broken, dropping the ` thinking`/` response`/`<search>` scaffold costs nothing — a correct direct answer still gets `1.0` (`score - structure_format_score`, with `structure_format_score=0`). There is no penalty for abandoning the recipe's structure, so the collapse is reward-optimal.
- The model converges to this shortcut: raw_reward climbs to a local optimum (~3% → ~27%) as responses shorten to the `<answer>…</answer>` minimum, but the held-out `eval/nq_test` metric **plateaus at ~16% EM** because the model is no longer learning to search or reason — it is memorizing/matching the most direct answer.

## Symptoms (not causes)

- **Response-length collapse**: rollout 1751 → ~10 tokens; eval 1569 → ~9.8 tokens.
- **Truncation collapse**: rollout 0.406 → 0; eval 0.381 → 0.
- **≈zero advantages**: `rollout/rewards` ~1e-9; `zero_std/count_0` ~20/32 per step.
- **Flat held-out eval**: `eval/nq_test` ~0.15–0.165 from step 69 → 199 (eval_first 0.048, eval_last 0.16467, eval_max 0.16567 in `outputs/metrics.json`).

(The `run_qwen2.5_3B.sh` showing `--num-rollout 200` vs. the recorded run's `num-rollout 3000` in `wandb/.../config.yaml` is a config inconsistency, but not causal here: the observed 0–199-step snapshot exhibits the same pathology regardless.)

# Diagnosis: Unhealthy

**Verdict:** The GRPO post-training run is **unhealthy**. Held-out validation accuracy
(`val-core/taco/acc/mean@1`) shows no improvement over training and in fact declined
from the zero-shot baseline.

## Root cause

**The binary (all-or-nothing) reward scoring function on the TACO code-generation
dataset provides an extremely sparse learning signal that is too weak to drive
meaningful improvement at the given step budget, batch size, and learning rate.**

## Causal chain

### 1. Binary reward collapses the per-sample signal

The custom reward function at `verl/utils/reward_score/taco.py:162` returns
`score = binary`, where `binary = 1.0` only when **every** hidden test case passes
and `0.0` otherwise. The average test case has many test assertions (the held-out
set contains problems with up to 275 tests per sample, as seen in the step-0
validation log line `n_pass/n_tests=0/275`). A model output that passes 273/275
tests receives zero reward — indistinguishable from a completely broken submission.

### 2. Low initial accuracy means most rollouts receive zero reward

- Initial validation accuracy (step 0, before training): **7.61%**
- Final validation accuracy (step 250): **5.43%**
- Training reward (`critic/score/mean`) at step 283: **7.03%**

At the initial accuracy level, proposed by the zero-shot base model `Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct`,
fewer than 1 in 13 rollouts earns a non-zero reward. With `rollout_n=8` samples per
prompt, the expected number of positive rewards in a mini-batch of 16 prompts is
roughly `16 × 8 × 0.076 = 9.7` out of 128 rollouts.

### 3. GRPO advantage normalization is dominated by noise

GRPO computes advantages by normalizing scores within each prompt group
(`norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo=True`). When most prompts receive zero rewards across all
8 rollouts, the advantage for that prompt group is a vector of zeros (no signal).
When a single rollout in a group gets a non-zero reward, the advantage signal is
driven by a single per-prompt outlier — the resulting updates are high-variance and
provide no reliable gradient direction.

Evidence: the logged advantages at step 283 have `critic/advantages/mean ≈ 0`,
confirming most rollouts sit near zero advantage. The `actor/pg_loss` hovers near
zero (-2.8e-5 to +5.2e-3) throughout training, and `actor/pg_clipfrac = 0.0` at
every logged step, indicating the policy gradient never produces meaningful updates.

### 4. KL divergence from reference stays near zero

`rollout_corr/kl ≈ 0.0007` throughout training, and `actor/ppo_kl = 0.0`. The
model barely moves from its initialization — the policy is not learning because
the loss landscape provides no usable gradient.

### 5. Training terminated early at step 284 (71% of budget)

The run logged its last step at step 284 (`wandb-summary.json` `_step=283`, log
shows step 284 entry) out of the 400-step budget — consistent with a run that was
stopped or timed out. But this is a symptom, not the cause: the dead gradient
meant the remaining 116 steps would not have rescued the run.

### 6. Pass rate confirms the model never improved code quality

`val-aux/taco/pass_rate/mean@1` (fraction of individual test cases passed)
oscillated between 0.176 and 0.226 across all validation checkpoints with no trend.
The model's ability to write correct code was flat from start to finish.

## Why this is a design defect and not just a hard problem

A binary `compute_score` is appropriate only when the base policy already achieves
a non-trivial success rate (ideally >30–50%) or when the rollout count per prompt
is very large (>>8) so that at least one non-zero reward per group is likely. For
this model–dataset pair (Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct on TACO with ~7.6% zero-shot
accuracy), the dense `pass_rate` score already computed inside `taco.py` would
provide a far more usable learning signal. The code at lines 164–168 explicitly
chooses `binary` over `pass_rate` as the `score` — this is the single decision
blocking learning.

## Supporting evidence

| Signal | Value | Interpretation |
|--------|-------|----------------|
| `val-core/taco/acc/mean@1` (step 0) | 0.0761 | Zero-shot baseline |

The run does not merely plateau — it converges to a policy that no longer performs the task it was trained on. By held-out evidence, eval/nq_test rose from 0.048 (step 0) to 0.1587 (step 69) and then oscillated in 0.148–0.166 for the remaining 130 steps (step 199: 0.1647) (`historical_evidence/eval_scores.json`, `wandb/latest-run/files/output.log`). A functioning Search-R1 agent must emit `<search>` and consume environment `<information>` over up to 8 turns; a ~9-token response can only be a direct closed-book answer. The ~0.16 EM plateau is consistent with the closed-book capacity of a 3B model, not with a working retrieval agent, and the held-out curve is flat from step ~69 onward while train raw_reward keeps drifting up (0.04 → 0.15–0.33; e.g. step 195: 0.336) — a train/held-out divergence that by itself rules out "healthy, just converged".

## Root cause (single, primary): observation tokens are trained on — `loss_mask` is 1 for environment-provided text

`examples/search-r1/generate_with_search.py` is the only training-logic file modified after the base snapshot (mtime 2026-11-04 vs. base 2026-10-21). At line 243 the environment's retrieval result — the `<information>…</information>` passages returned by the tool, tokens the *policy never generated* — is appended with

```python
loss_mask += [1] * len(obs_tokens_ids)          # upstream slime uses [0]
```

and at line 259 `sample.loss_mask = loss_mask` overwrites the internally-built mask, so the `[1]` survives into training. Upstream slime's equivalent is `[0] * len(obs_tokens_ids)` (cf. `slime/utils/types.py:292`, `Sample.append_response_tokens`: `[1 if trainable else 0] * len(tokens)` — the same file demonstrates the correct convention that `trainable=False` must mask out). The mask is not cosmetic: the policy-gradient reducer is `(x_i * loss_mask_i).sum() / clamp(denom, 1)` per sample (`slime/backends/megatron_utils/cp_utils.py:76`), i.e. **loss_mask=1 tokens receive policy-gradient credit**, and each retrieval chunk is ~300–600 high-entropy tokens versus ~10 low-entropy model tokens.

Causal chain from this one defect to every observed pathology:

1. **Polluted credit assignment.** The trajectory-level group advantage (all 0/1 EM, `rollout/raw_reward`) is broadcast to every unmasked token. With obs tokens masked in, the dense, easy-to-model Wikipedia text absorbs the gradient. Because obs text is identical across the 8 samples of a GRPO group (same prompt → same retrieval), the model is pushed to *raise* likelihood of environment text — probability mass it can only realize by producing retrieval-like text or by terminating turns so the environment emits it. This is the mechanism behind the length collapse: response_len falls monotonically 1751 → 1468 → 962 → 197 → 33 → 10.2 tokens within the first 50 steps (`wandb output.log`), truncated_ratio 0.406 → 0.0 — the model abandons `<search>` entirely because emitting `<answer>…</answer>` immediately (a) ends the episode before any obs tokens accrue, and (b) still collects the group-centered reward.
2. **Reward becomes format-blind.** `qa_em_format.compute_score_em` is effectively pure 0/1 EM: the `format_score=0.2` argument is dead (never used in the function), and `structure_format_score`/`final_format_score`/`retrieval_score` default to 0, so a *correct answer in invalid format still scores 1.0* (`score - structure_format_score = 1 - 0`). With format pressure removed, RL optimizes "shortest path to EM" = closed-book answering, and the eval-side length collapse (1568 → 9.8) confirms the same behavior generalizes held-out.
3. **Held-out plateau.** Closed-book answering saturates at the model's parametric-knowledge ceiling (~0.16 for NQ-style questions at 3B). Steps 69–199 show zero trend (0.148, 0.1487, 0.1543, 0.1497, 0.1503, 0.1583, 0.1617, 0.1617, 0.1527, 0.1583, 0.1560, 0.1657, 0.1647), while `rollout_log_probs` keeps drifting (-1.13 → -0.35) — the policy keeps changing (still absorbing obs-token gradients) but held-out EM does not: the run is optimizing something other than task quality.

## Secondary root cause: added engine-level stop tags mask the format failure and lock the short-answer policy in

The same modified file adds `"stop": ["</search>", "</answer>"]` to the sglang sampling params (lines 164–177), described as a "BUGFIX" for junk tokens after the tags. Whatever its intent, its observable effect is to make every generation terminate cleanly at the first `</answer>` — so truncated_ratio → 0.0 and the format state machine (`is_valid_sequence`) rarely fails, hiding the degradation that step-0 behavior (38% truncation, resp_len 1751) showed was being selected against. It also makes the short-answer attractor cheap to execute: a ~9-token `<think>…</think><answer>…</answer>` response always completes, always parses, and under the EM-only reward is rewarded whenever the guess is right. From step ~50 onward the rollout statistics are frozen (zero_std groups: 20–27 of 32 prompts per batch get all-identical 0/1 rewards → zero advantage; `rollout/zero_std/count_0 ≈ 25`, occasionally `count_1.0: 1`), so learning is driven by a handful of groups per step replaying the same signal.

## Symptoms (not causes) — and why they are not the defect

- `rollout/rewards ≈ 1e-9` at every step while `raw_reward` is 0.04–0.33: this is the **group-centered mean** (`rewards - mean` per GRPO group, `slime/ray/rollout.py:742-755`); the mean of group-centered rewards is ~0 by construction. It is a logging artifact, not a broken reward.
- `rollout/kl = 0.0` exactly, every step: `args.kl_coef=0.0` (config.yaml), so `compute_advantages_and_returns` short-circuits to zero tensors (`loss.py:751`); the KL penalty actually active is `use_kl_loss=true, kl_loss_coef=0.001, low_var_kl` inside the loss. Not a defect, but it means nothing restrained the drift once the reward signal degenerated.
- `rollout_log_probs ≈ -1.12` vs `ref_log_probs ≈ -1.68` at step 0: obs tokens carry dummy log-probs `[0.0]` (`generate_with_search.py:248`), pulling the rollout average up; part of the same obs-token mishandling family, but a metric artifact rather than an independent fault.
- `experiment_logs/cybertron-751761.log` (2004 lines) is entirely teleport session-upload 403 noise (`InvalidAccessKeyId`); `…stderr.log` is 2 empty lines. The logs are uninformative but harmless — infrastructure, not training, failure.
- The train/eval length collapse, truncation collapse, and zero_std counts are the *observable behavior* of the two root causes above, not independent defects.

## Summary of the causal chain

loss_mask=1 on environment `<information>` tokens (root cause 1) + EM-only, format-blind reward (root cause 2) + engine stop tags ensuring clean short completions (root cause 3) → policy-gradient credit for text the model never generated and no penalty for abandoning search → within 50 steps the policy collapses to ~10-token direct answers, search behavior is extinguished, truncation hits 0, GRPO groups go reward-degenerate (zero advantage for 75–85% of prompts) → held-out EM plateaus at the closed-book ceiling (~0.16) from step 69 onward while train reward keeps rising → a Search-R1 run that no longer searches, i.e. an unhealthy experiment whose frozen held-out evidence (plateau + length collapse) and only-modified-file forensics agree on the same mechanism.

The pipeline is mechanically intact (no crash, rewards computed and flowing, weight sync verified), but the run produced **no learning**: held-out accuracy never left baseline and training reward stayed flat while the policy drifted degenerately (response length ×2.5, entropy up). This is a failed training run, not a stalled-but-healthy one.

## Held-out evidence (primary)
`val-core/taco/acc/mean@1` at steps 0/50/100/150/200/250 (output.log, 184-problem test set, temp 0.7 sampling):
**0.0761, 0.0489, 0.0598, 0.0707, 0.0435, 0.0543** — no trend; all within ±1σ (σ ≈ 0.0175) of the ~0.06 baseline. Six evaluations, zero improvement.
Training reward agrees: `critic/score/mean` flat at ~0.12 (20-step windows 0.093–0.148, first 0.125 / last 0.148 — noise).

## Root causes

**1. Effective optimization is one tiny gradient step per rollout over a sub-epoch of data.**
`verl/trainer/ppo/ray_trainer.py:1351-1359` (`_update_actor`): `ppo_mini_batch_size = 16 × rollout.n(8) = 128` = the entire repeated global batch, with `ppo_epochs=1` → exactly **one optimizer step per training step**. Effective config: constant `actor.lr = 1e-06` (all 281 logged steps `actor/lr:1e-06` — no warmup/decay). 283 steps × 16 prompts = 4,528 unique prompts of 8,368 in `taco_verl/train.parquet` (`training/epoch 0` in wandb-summary) — under one epoch, each prompt seen once. Total: ~283 low-LR Adam steps of policy-gradient on a sparse signal.

**2. The reward signal is almost entirely zero-advantage.**
`verl/utils/reward_score/taco.py:125` (`_summarize`): `binary = 1.0 if n_pass == n else 0.0` — all-or-nothing; the computed `pass_rate` is discarded. At the observed ~12% solve rate, ≥ 0.88^8 ≈ **36% of 8-rollout groups are all-fail** (harder problems approach 100%), and all-pass groups are also zero-advantage — GRPO group normalization (`norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo=true`, uid-indexed, epsilon-guarded in core_algos.py:268) gives exactly zero gradient for every homogeneous group. The model gets no signal on precisely the problems it cannot yet solve.

**3. Sandbox scoring zeroes slow-but-correct solutions (reward-signal suppressor).**
`taco.py:275` module global `timeout = 4` drives the per-case `signal.alarm` (line 327), while the global join cap is `min(max(10, 4·n_cases+1), 120)` (line 95): for many-test problems (logged case `n_tests=275`) even a correct sequential solution exceeds 120s → `[-1]*n` + `global_timeout` → score 0. Evidence: `[TACO-FAIL]` blocks with plausible code ending `[error] global_timeout`, and `timing_s/agent_loop/compute_score/max = 121.18s` pinned at the 120s cap.

**4. Nothing anchors the policy while it drifts.**
Effective overrides: `use_kl_loss=False`, `kl_loss_coef=0`, `entropy_coeff=0`, `algorithm.use_kl_in_reward=False`. With no KL, entropy, or length penalty, the sparse noisy gradients from (1)+(2) produce free drift instead of improvement.

## Causal chain
Weak single-step updates (1) acting on a reward that is zero for ~all homogeneous groups and miscalibrated for slow solutions (2, 3), with no regularizer (4) → the policy moves (entropy 0.47→0.57, grad_norm 0.38→0.17, response length 174→~440 tokens across 20-step windows) but the movement is **not reward-directed**: score and held-out accuracy stay flat while outputs inflate — length drift without competence gain, the signature of noise accumulation rather than learning.

## Symptoms (not root causes)
- Flat val acc and flat `critic/score/mean` — outcomes of the above.
- `actor/ppo_kl = 0.0` and `actor/pg_clipfrac = 0` at **every** step: arithmetically expected for fully on-policy single-epoch updates (`old_log_prob` recomputed at current weights → ratio ≡ 1; `pg_loss = -2.8e-5` exactly mirrors `advantages/mean = 2.8e-5`). **Not a defect** — do not treat as evidence of broken updates.
- Length/entropy/grad_norm drift — symptom of unanchored noise.
- Run stopped at step 283/400 after 28,629.5s (~7.95h at ~137s/step; 400 steps would need ~15h); no Traceback/OOM in output.log — consistent with an external wall-clock stop, which per the task is not by itself proof of a defect. Consequence: `save_freq=400` was never reached, so no checkpoint exists (outputs/ contains only `.hydra/` and `main_ppo.log`).

## Checked and ruled out
- `tool_calls=0` / `num_turns=2`: hardcoded schema constant in `single_turn_agent_loop.py`, not multi-turn breakage.
- Weight-sync staleness: `rollout_actor_probs_pearson_corr 0.99947`, `rollout_probs_diff_valid=1`.

- Truncation: `response_length/clip_ratio 0`, `aborted_ratio 0`, `prompt clip_ratio 0`.
- Data ordering: `data.shuffle: true` → `RandomSampler` (ppo/utils.py:158) — length drift is not a prompt-order artifact.
- `num_preempted: -1`: vLLM sentinel, not a real count.

# RL Training Run Diagnosis

## Verdict

**Unhealthy.** The staged Search-R1 post-training run is **unhealthy**. Although held-out evaluation score (`eval/nq_test`) increases from `0.048` at step 0 to `0.1587` at step 69 and then plateaus around `0.148–0.1657` through step 199 (`0.1647` at step 199), the policy has collapsed into a degenerate single-turn parametric-answering behavior (`<answer> ... </answer>` without `<think>` or `<search>`), completely abandoning multi-turn reasoning and search retrieval.

---

## Root Causes

There are three concrete bugs in the Search-R1 rollout and reward implementation (`examples/search-r1/generate_with_search.py` and `examples/search-r1/qa_em_format.py`) that jointly cause this failure and prevent multi-turn search from being learned:

### 1. Broken format-reward wiring and zeroed format/retrieval reward parameters (`generate_with_search.py` & `qa_em_format.py`)
In `examples/search-r1/generate_with_search.py:287-291`, `reward_func` calls `compute_score_em` passing `format_score=SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["format_score"]` (`0.2`):
```python
score = compute_score_em(
    solution_str=sample.prompt + sample.response,
    ground_truth=sample.label["ground_truth"],
    format_score=SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["format_score"],
)
```
However, in `examples/search-r1/qa_em_format.py:156-208`, `compute_score_em` has default parameters `structure_format_score=0`, `final_format_score=0`, `retrieval_score=0`, `format_score=0`, `score=1.0`, and **never uses `format_score` anywhere in its body**:
- When `answer` is incorrect or `None` with valid format (`is_valid_format == True`), it returns `structure_format_score + retrieval_score` (`0 + 0 = 0`) or `structure_format_score` (`0`).
- When `answer` matches ground truth (`em_check == 1`), it returns `score` (`1.0`) if `is_valid_format` is `True`, and `score - structure_format_score` (`1.0 - 0 = 1.0`) if `is_valid_format` is `False`.

**Direct Effect:**
1. The reward function is strictly binary (`0` or `1.0`) based solely on Exact Match (`em_check`), confirmed across all 200 training steps in `wandb/offline-run-20260821_033838-wi4fh8cz/files/output.log`: `rollout/zero_std` only ever contains `count_0` and `count_1.0` (never `0.1`, `0.2`, `0.3`, or `0.8`), and `rollout/raw_reward * 256` is an exact integer at every step.
2. There is **zero reward shaping** for producing valid `<think>...</think><search>...</search>` structure or retrieving the right document (`retrieval_score=0`), and **zero penalty** (`structure_format_score=0`) for violating the sequence format (`is_valid_sequence`) when outputting a direct `<answer>...</answer>` without `<think>` tags.

### 2. Retrieval document body text discarded before being shown to the model (`generate_with_search.py`)
In `examples/search-r1/generate_with_search.py:44-56`, `_passages2string` parses each retrieved document (`"Title"\nText...`) into `title` and `text`, but omits `text` when constructing the observation string:
```python
def _passages2string(retrieval_result):
    format_reference = ""
    for idx, doc_item in enumerate(retrieval_result):
        content = doc_item["document"]["contents"]
        title = content.split("\n")[0]
        text = "\n".join(content.split("\n")[1:])
        format_reference += f"Doc {idx+1}(Title: {title})\n"

    return format_reference
```
**Direct Effect:** Every `<information>...</information>` block returned from `search()` contains only document titles (`Doc 1(Title: ...)\nDoc 2(Title: ...)\nDoc 3(Title: ...)`), discarding the passage contents (`text`). Consequently, calling `<search>` provides almost no factual information to help answer questions, while consuming turns and token budget (and risking truncation at `rollout_max_response_len = 1024`).

### 3. Observation tokens remain unmasked (`loss_mask = 1`) during policy gradient training (`generate_with_search.py`)
In `examples/search-r1/generate_with_search.py:219-259`, although `sample.append_response_tokens` is called with `trainable=True` for model turns (line 224) and `trainable=False` for environment observations (line 244), `generate()` maintains its own local `loss_mask` list where **both** model tokens (line 219) and environment observation tokens `obs_tokens_ids` (line 243) are appended with `[1] * len(...)`:
```python
obs_tokens_ids = state.tokenizer(next_obs, add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"]
response += next_obs
response_token_ids += obs_tokens_ids
loss_mask += [1] * len(obs_tokens_ids)
sample.append_response_tokens(args, tokens=obs_tokens_ids, trainable=False)
```
Then, at line 259, `generate()` overwrites `sample.loss_mask` constructed by `append_response_tokens`:
```python
sample.loss_mask = loss_mask
```
**Direct Effect:** All environment-injected `<information>...</information>` and invalid-action feedback tokens have `loss_mask = 1` (verified in `output.log`, where `perf/tokens_per_gpu_per_sec` and `perf/effective_tokens_per_gpu_per_sec`—which sum `response_length` and `sum(loss_mask)` respectively—are identical at every single step, e.g., `2228.4869` at step 0). Because failed multi-turn search rollouts have negative GRPO advantages and predominantly consist of observation tokens, the policy gradient updates the model on environment tokens and strongly penalizes trajectories that trigger `<search>`.

---

## Causal Chain and Observed Workspace Evidence

1. **Initial Multi-Turn Exploration Fails to Yield Useful Evidence (Steps 0–10):**
   - At step 0 (`outputs/historical_eval_trace.log`, `wandb/.../output.log`), the initial Qwen2.5-3B model attempts multi-turn reasoning and search, producing long trajectories (`eval/nq_test/response_len/mean = 1568.6`, `rollout/response_len/mean = 1751.5`, `max = 13912`) with high truncation (`eval/nq_test/truncated_ratio = 0.3813`, `rollout/truncated_ratio = 0.40625`).
   - Because `_passages2string` strips passage bodies and only returns document titles, searching fails to surface answers (`eval/nq_test = 0.048`, `rollout/raw_reward = 0.0391`).
   - Because `format_score` is ignored and `structure_format_score = 0` / `retrieval_score = 0` in `compute_score_em`, well-formatted multi-turn search trajectories that fail to guess the exact answer receive `0` reward, and their unmasked observation tokens (`loss_mask = 1`) receive negative policy gradients.

2. **Rapid Length Collapse into Direct Parametric Guessing (Steps 10–69):**
   - When the model occasionally skips `<think>` and `<search>` and immediately emits `<answer> ... </answer>` ( referencing the prompt's one-shot example `For example, <answer> Beijing </answer>`), if its parametric knowledge matches the NQ answer, `compute_score_em` returns `score - structure_format_score = 1.0 - 0 = 1.0` even though `is_valid_sequence` is `False` (missing `<think>`).
   - GRPO strongly reinforces this short, format-invalid `<answer> ... </answer>` pattern because it avoids truncation and achieves non-zero reward.
   - In `wandb/.../output.log`, median training response length (`rollout/response_len/median`) collapses from `1099.5` tokens (step 0) -> `588.5` (step 10) -> `129.0` (step 13) -> `56.5` (step 14) -> `12.0` (step 16) -> `10.0` (step 19) -> `9.0` tokens (step 22 onwards).
   - Similarly, on held-out evaluation (`outputs/historical_eval_trace.log`), `eval/nq_test/response_len/mean` drops from `1568.6` (step 0) -> `272.0` (step 19, median `11.0`) -> `25.0` (step 49) -> `14.1` (step 59). A 7–10 token response in the Qwen2.5 tokenizer corresponds to a bare `<answer> ... </answer>` span with zero `<think>` or `<search>` turns.

3. **Deceptive Metric Improvement Followed by Premature Plateau (Steps 69–199):**
   - Eliminating multi-turn search and truncation allows the model to collect parametric-knowledge exact matches on easy questions, causing `eval/nq_test` to rise initially from `0.048` (step 0) to `0.1587` (step 69) while `eval/nq_test/truncated_ratio` drops from `0.3813` to `0.0003`.
   - From step 69 to step 199, `eval/nq_test` stagnates between `0.148` and `0.1657` (ending at `0.1647` at step 199 with `eval/nq_test/response_len/mean = 9.76` tokens and `rollout/response_len/mean = 9.25`, `max = 18` tokens at step 199). Without functional passage retrieval or format enforcement, the model is permanently stuck as a closed-book 1-turn QA guesser and cannot reach healthy Search-R1 retrieval-augmented performance.

---

## Distinction Between Root Causes and Symptoms

- **Root Causes:**
  1. `compute_score_em` in `examples/search-r1/qa_em_format.py:156-208` leaves `structure_format_score=0`, `final_format_score=0`, `retrieval_score=0` and ignores the `format_score=0.2` argument passed by `reward_func` (`generate_with_search.py:290`), removing all format/retrieval reward shaping and granting full `1.0` reward to unformatted `<answer>...</answer>` responses.
  2. `_passages2string` in `examples/search-r1/generate_with_search.py:54` formats only `Doc {idx+1}(Title: {title})\n` and drops `text`, starving the model of retrieved passage content.
  3. `generate` in `examples/search-r1/generate_with_search.py:243,259` sets `loss_mask += [1] * len(obs_tokens_ids)` and overwrites `sample.loss_mask = loss_mask`, training the policy on non-model observation tokens.
- **Symptoms (Observed Consequences, Not Root Causes):**
  - Collapse of `rollout/response_len/mean` (from `1751.5` to `~9–10` tokens) and `eval/nq_test/response_len/mean` (from `1568.6` to `9.76` tokens), and collapse of `truncated_ratio` from `~0.40` to `0.0`.
  - The initial rise of `eval/nq_test` (`0.048 -> 0.1587`) and `rollout/raw_reward` (`0.039 -> ~0.17–0.25`) as the policy stops truncating on useless title-only searches and switches to direct closed-book `<answer>` emission, followed by a hard plateau at `~0.15–0.165` from step 69 to step 199.
  - Note: The log cutoff at step 200 / eval step 199 (`historical_evidence/manifest.json`) and the S3 session-upload warnings in `experiment_logs/cybertron-751761.log` are benign harness/infrastructure artifacts and not causes of the training pathology.

### 1. Severe Prompt–Test Harness Mismatch and Unsolvable Ground Truth in `taco_verl/train.parquet`
A large fraction of the training dataset (`taco_verl/train.parquet`, 8,368 rows) has contradictory prompt instructions and ground-truth evaluation formats in `verl/utils/reward_score/taco.py`:
- **Call-based prompts mislabeled as `stdin` (1,471 / 8,368 rows, 17.6% of training data; 24.5% of `stdin` rows):** These GeeksforGeeks-style problems explicitly instruct the model *"You don't need to read input or print anything. Your task is to complete the function ... #User function Template for python3 / class Solution: ... \nUse Call-Based format"*. However, their `ground_truth` has `fn_name: null` (`extra_info.code_type == "stdin"`). In `taco.py:304-375`, `fn_name is None` routes execution to `CODE_TYPE.standard_input`, which wraps the model's code inside `def code():`, calls `code()`, and captures `sys.stdout`. Because the model follows the prompt and defines `class Solution` without reading stdin or printing, `code()` defines the class and exits with `output = []`, receiving a deterministic reward of `0.0` (e.g., `train6`, `train8927`, `train9403`, `train2056`). Furthermore, 1,312 of these rows have raw assignment strings in `ground_truth["inputs"]` (such as `'N = 6\nArr[] = {-3, -2, 0, 3, 4, 5}'`), which do not match standard competitive-programming stdin formats.
- **Unparsed/corrupted `call_based` ground-truth inputs and outputs (147 + 165 rows in `train.parquet`):**
  - In **147 `call_based` rows** (e.g., `train46`, `train48`, `train87`, `train24805`, `train6391`), `fn_name` is set, so `taco.py:440` executes `method(*inputs)`. However, `inputs` in `ground_truth` is a multi-line string (e.g., `'2\nabcdefh\nbcd\n...'`) rather than a JSON list of arguments. Unpacking `*inputs` passes each character of the string as a separate positional argument, raising `TypeError: searchPattern() takes 2 positional arguments but 25 were given` (step 183) or `isBinary() takes 1 positional argument but 9 were given` (step 51).
  - In **46 `call_based` rows** (mostly LeetCode-style `class Solution` prompts, e.g., `train12339`, `train155`, `train392`), string arguments and expected outputs are double-JSON-encoded with literal quote characters inside the string (e.g., `input = ["\"abcd\"", "\"abcde\""]`).

The reward function (`taco.py`) has three defects that corrupt the reward signal and dominate step runtime:
- **All-or-nothing binary reward discarding partial test-case signal (`taco.py:125, 147-159`):** `compute_score` sets `score = binary` (`1.0` only if `n_pass == n`, else `0.0`), even though `pass_rate = n_pass / n` is computed right above it. In TACO, many problems have dozens or hundreds of test cases (median 206.5 tests in `test.parquet`, up to 1,440 in `train.parquet`). Across logged training failures, **29.7% (166/559)** passed a subset of test cases (`n_pass > 0`) but received `0.0` reward, starving GRPO of dense progress signal and causing zero-advantage groups when all 8 rollouts partially pass or fail.
- **Unprotected execution of top-level example/test calls (`taco.py:323-388`):**
  - For `call_based` problems (`taco.py:329`), `exec(compile(sol, ...))` executes the entire generated snippet at module import before calling `method(*inputs)`.   - For `standard_input` problems (`taco.py:346-375`), `run_test` indents every non-import line into `def code():`. Any `# Example usage` call at the bottom of the snippet runs inside `code()` on every test case and prints hardcoded sample outputs to `stdout`, corrupting the captured output even when the function logic is otherwise relevant.
- **Broken markdown fence extraction in `post_process` (`taco.py:38-47`) coupled with prompt format:** Every prompt instructs: ``Your ANSWER should be in a code block format like this: ```python # Write your code here ```.`` When the model echoes the inline placeholder `` ```python # Write your code here ``` `` before its actual solution fence, or puts code on the first line after `` ```python ``, `post_process` extracts only `blocks[0]` (the empty placeholder `# Write your code here`) or fails to strip the `python` language tag when `blocks[0]` starts with a newline (`if not text.startswith("\n"):`), leaving a bare `python` identifier that crashes with `NameError: name 'python' is not defined`.
- **Sequential per-case timeouts without early exit on `TimeoutException` (`taco.py:95, 291-505`):** Each test case sets `signal.alarm(4)`, but on timeout `run_test` catches `Exception`, appends `-1`, and **continues looping through all remaining test cases** until the outer process timeout (`min(max(10, 4 * n_cases + 1), 120)` seconds, plus 1s join) kills the worker at **~121.2 seconds**.

# Verdict: unhealthy

The GRPO actor is not trained on the outcome advantages of the sequences that earned them. `compute_grpo_outcome_advantage` group-normalizes correctly, then broadcasts one scrambled row across the batch. Held-out accuracy never recovers the base model, and the optimization traces show a policy that barely moves.

## Root cause

The live path is the legacy trainer (`trainer.use_v1: false` in the W&B config for `offline-run-20260926_105216-l7my3znq`). `algorithm.adv_estimator` is `grpo` with `norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo: true`, so `RayPPOTrainer.compute_advantage` calls `compute_grpo_outcome_advantage` in `verl/trainer/ppo/core_algos.py`. The vectorized estimator, which does `scalars.unsqueeze(-1) * response_mask`, is registered only for `grpo_vectorized` and is not used.

Group normalization itself is right. Scores are summed over tokens, grouped by `uid` (rollout `n: 8`), and whitened with the unbiased group standard deviation. For binary 0/1 outcomes that produces a known set of scalars: one success in eight is about `+2.47486673 / −0.35355239`; four of eight is about `±0.93541260`; a uniform group is 0. Every logged `critic/advantages/max` and `min` is one of those eight values (or 0). Step 283 is exactly `advantages/max = 2.4748666286468506` and `advantages/min = −0.935412585735321`.

The next lines throw that vector away as a per-sequence advantage. With batch size 128 and `max_response_length` 4096:

```python
row = scores.reshape(1, -1)          # (1, 128)
row = pad(row, to response_length)    # (1, 4096), tail zeros
scores = row.expand(bsz, -1) * response_mask
```

Every sequence receives the same prefix of the batch score vector, masked by its own response length. Sequence `i` does not get `scores[i]` on its tokens. `metric_utils` then takes a masked max/min over that tensor, so the logged extrema still show the raw group scalars. Those extrema are evidence that normalization ran, not that the actor was credited for the right samples.

The reward makes the misalignment decisive. `taco.compute_score` returns a binary all-tests-pass `score` (and the same value as `acc`). `NaiveRewardManager` writes that scalar only onto the last valid response token. Policy loss is token-mean PPO (`loss_agg_mode: token-mean`, clip 0.2, `ppo_epochs: 1`). The gradient at the reinforced token is therefore whatever foreign scalar landed at index `L-1`: `scores[L-1]` when `L <= 128`, else 0. A sequence carries its own advantage there only when its response length is `i+1`. On 2000 simulated batches of 128 (pass rate 0.12, lengths near the observed mean), that happens on about 0.11% of sequences. Mean absolute last-token advantage is about 0.06, against about 0.45 if each sequence kept its own scalar.

## Causal chain

1. Training reward is sparse and real. `critic/score/mean` window averages stay about 0.125 (steps 1–20), 0.115, 0.127, 0.133, 0.129, 0.122, then 0.093 (steps 251–284). `score/max` still hits 1. So some rollouts fully pass, and mixed groups of eight do produce the ±2.47 / ±0.94 advantages above.
2. Those advantages are not aligned to the passing sequences. Token-mean `actor/pg_loss` equals `-critic/advantages/mean` on all 280 logged update steps (difference under `1e-6`), and that mean stays near 0 (absolute mean about `3e-4`, largest absolute mean about 0.014). `actor/pg_clipfrac` and `actor/ppo_kl` are 0 on every update. Rollout-vs-train KL stays about `5e-4` and probability Pearson correlation about 0.9995 through step 284. Gradients stay finite (window means about 0.38 down to 0.18). There is no NaN, OOM, or traceback.
3. With `use_kl_loss: false`, `kl_loss_coef: 0`, `use_kl_in_reward: false`, and `entropy_coeff: 0`, nothing else anchors the policy. The only behavioral drift is longer, slightly higher-entropy samples under train temperature 1.0: response length about 174 → about 440, entropy about 0.47 → about 0.56. Response clip is 0 except five steps at `1/128`. Prompt clip is 0.
4. Held-out `val-core/taco/acc/mean@1` (184 problems, `n: 1`, temperature 0.7, same binary `acc`) starts at 0.07609 (14/184) before training and is then 0.04891 (9), 0.05978 (11), 0.07065 (13), 0.04348 (8), and 0.05435 (10) at steps 50, 100, 150, 200, and 250. Every eval is below the base model; the best later eval is 13/184. `pass_rate` stays roughly flat (0.195 → peak 0.226 at step 150 → 0.195 at step 250) because it is not the optimized reward. Train binary reward does not rise either, so this is not a train/val metric mismatch.

## Symptoms, not causes

- The log stops at step 284 of `total_training_steps: 400` after a complete metric line. A later reprint of steps 211–212 is logger reorder. `save_freq` is 400, so no checkpoint is expected. Truncation did not create the flat loss or the earlier val drop.
- `timing_s/gen` is often ~120s (172/280 steps over 100s) because `compute_score/max` is ~121s on 171/280 steps while the mean score time is ~2s. Large TACO suites (held-out median ~200 tests, per-case alarm 4s, global cap 120s) slow the step. They do not zero the policy gradient.
- The launch script defaults to 8 GPUs; this host ran 4. That changes throughput only.
- Train problems have far fewer tests than the held-out set (median 5 vs ~200). That makes `pass_rate` look healthier than binary `acc`. It does not explain `pg_loss ≈ 0` while advantage extrema sit at the full group-normalized values.
- Logged TACO failures are a cap of two samples per step, mostly `result=False` wrong answers, not scorer exceptions. Val `n=1` on 184 items is noisy, but five consecutive evals below 14/184, together with a train reward that never trends up and a policy KL that never leaves ~1e-3, is failed learning.

# Diagnosis: slime Search-R1 Qwen2.5-3B GRPO run (steps 0–200)

## Verdict: UNHEALTHY

The run is a textbook case of reward-driven behavioral collapse. Held-out NQ EM rises from 0.048 to only ~0.165 and flatlines from step ~70 through step 199, while the policy abandons retrieval entirely: median response length collapses from ~1100 tokens to 9 tokens (a bare `<answer>X</answer>`) by step ~20 and stays there. The model converges to closed-book guessing — the exact opposite of what Search-R1 training is supposed to produce — and held-out accuracy saturates at the base model's closed-book ceiling instead of a retrieval-augmented level.

## Evidence

Frozen eval trace (`outputs/historical_eval_trace.log`, `historical_evidence/eval_scores.json`, wandb run `wi4fh8cz`):
- `eval/nq_test`: 0.048 → 0.159 (step 69) → oscillates 0.148–0.166 through step 199. No improvement for the last ~130 steps.
- `eval/nq_test/response_len/mean`: 1568 → 272 (step 19) → 25 (step 49) → ~10 tokens from step 60 on; median 9.0. Nine tokens is exactly `<answer> X </answer>` + EOS — no `<think>`, no `<search>`, no retrieval.
- Train rollouts mirror this: `rollout/response_len/mean` 1751 → ~10 by step 50; `rollout/truncated_ratio` 0.41 → 0.0; prefix-cache hit rate falls 0.76 → 0.24 (rollouts stop sharing retrieved-document prefixes because retrieval stops happening).
- Meanwhile `rollout/raw_reward` keeps climbing (0.04 → ~0.2–0.3) — training reward improves while held-out EM stagnates, so the reward being optimized is not measuring search-augmented task success.

## Root cause: the reward function only pays for a correct final answer; every format/retrieval partial credit is dead code

`examples/search-r1/generate_with_search.py::reward_func` calls

```python
compute_score_em(solution_str=sample.prompt + sample.response,
                 ground_truth=..., format_score=SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["format_score"])  # 0.2
```

but in `examples/search-r1/qa_em_format.py`, `format_score` appears only in the signature and docstring — no return path uses it. All partial credit flows through `structure_format_score`, `retrieval_score`, and `final_format_score`, which the call site never sets, so they default to 0. The in-code comments (`# 0.3`, `# 0.2`, `# 0.1`) show the intended shaping, but as wired the reward is binary:

- 1.0 iff the extracted last `<answer>` exactly matches a golden answer (0.8 if "format-invalid" — irrelevant since the 1.0 path dominates),
- 0 otherwise — including a perfectly formatted `<think>…</think><search>…</search>…<answer>wrong</answer>` trajectory, which scores exactly the same as garbage.

A secondary quirk makes the extraction "work" for single-answer outputs: `extract_solution` returns `None` unless there are ≥2 `<answer>…</answer>` matches, but `solution_str` is `sample.prompt + sample.response`, and the instruction prompt itself contains the example `<answer> Beijing </answer>`. So the model's single answer plus the prompt's example satisfy the ≥2 rule and the model's own answer (the last match) is scored. The net effect is not a broken scorer but a purely EM-based one.

## Causal chain

1. Reward is binary EM on the final answer; searching earns nothing extra, and a correct answer found via retrieval pays exactly the same 1.0 as a closed-book guess that happens to be right.
2. At step 0 the base model attempts multi-turn search: mean response ~1750 tokens, 38–41% of samples truncate (8-turn loop, up to 1024 new tokens *per turn* — `max_new_tokens` is never decremented across turns in `generate_with_search.generate` — plus 3 retrieved documents per turn against an 8129-token context). Truncated samples have no complete `<answer>` → reward 0.
3. Under GRPO group normalization (`n_samples_per_prompt=8`, `grpo_filter_groups_with_same_reward=false`), most groups are all-zero (~20–26 of 32 prompts per batch have zero advantage variance: `rollout/zero_std/count_0`), so the only persistent gradient comes from prompts the model can already answer closed-book. On those, short direct answers have strictly lower truncation/variance risk than long search trajectories at equal reward, so GRPO systematically selects for them.
4. Policy collapses to `<answer>guess</answer>` within ~20 steps; retrieval is never reinforced, so eval EM converges to the closed-book NQ ability of Qwen2.5-3B (~0.16 at temperature 1.0 — eval inherits `rollout_temperature=1.0` since `--eval-temperature` is unset) and stays there. The continuing rise in `rollout/raw_reward` after the eval plateau reflects the train split being easier and the policy sharpening its guesses — reward improvement without capability improvement.

## Symptoms (not root causes)

- The early 38–41% truncation ratio is a contributing pressure (it makes long trajectories score 0), not an independent defect; it follows from the per-turn token budget interacting with a base model that rambles at temperature 1.0.
- The truncated/short log and `rollout/kl = 0.0` throughout are consistent with the collapse (responses too short to accumulate measurable KL), not evidence of an optimization failure; the optimizer itself appears to have run cleanly for all 200 steps (`first_rollout_ok`, complete metric series, no crashes in the wandb output log).
- The infrastructure workarounds in `run_qwen2.5_3B.sh` (retriever reuse, no_proxy, ulimit) are unrelated to the training pathology.

Thus no evaluation exceeds baseline, and the final recorded result is **10/184 correct versus 14/184 initially**. Auxiliary mean per-test pass rate rises through step 150 but returns to **0.1952 at step 250 versus 0.1951 at baseline**. Individual sampled evaluations are noisy, but the complete trajectory provides no evidence of durable improvement.

## Root causes

1. **The optimized reward discards partial correctness, producing a sparse and often uninformative GRPO signal.** The launch script and effective Hydra overrides select `reward.custom_reward_function.name=compute_score` from `verl/utils/reward_score/taco.py`. That entry point computes both outcomes but assigns `score = binary`, where binary is 1 only when every test passes; `pass_rate` is merely auxiliary. The naive reward manager uses `score` as the token-level training reward. With GRPO and eight responses per prompt, all-equal rewards within a prompt group yield zero relative advantage, regardless of whether some responses pass more individual tests.

   This is visible in behavior, not just implementation: across 280 captured training rows, mean binary score is about **0.122**, so roughly **87.8% of responses receive zero reward**; average score is **0.127 over steps 1–25 but 0.093 over steps 251–284**. Steps 18, 132, and 209 have exactly zero gradient norm, direct extreme cases of uninformative batches. This reward bottleneck explains why updates can occur without useful held-out progress. The held-out data are especially demanding for all-tests success: they average **204.4 tests/problem versus 40.8 in training**, consistent with the large gap between exact accuracy and partial pass rate.

2. **Test scoring repeatedly hits its global timeout, dominating runtime and potentially destroying partial results.** `taco.py` caps the whole-solution wait at `min(max(10, 4*n_tests + 1), 120)` seconds and joins for one additional second. On global timeout it records `global_timeout` and failure for every test rather than retaining partial passes. The logs contain explicit `global_timeout` failures, and **166/280 training steps** have maximum sample-scoring time above 120 seconds, commonly about **121 seconds**. Slow steps show roughly 123–127 seconds of generation and 136–140 seconds total, versus roughly 17–32 seconds for fast steps. The summary records about **7.95 hours** of runtime while only reaching approximately step 284 of the configured 400. This timeout path is a concrete runtime defect and can further sparsify rewards, although the incomplete capture does not establish why the run ultimately stopped.

## Symptoms and ruled-out explanations

- The evidence contains training through about step 284, with out-of-order and missing metric lines. There is no traceback, OOM, NaN metric, or explicit termination record; the incomplete log and absent step-400 checkpoint are **symptoms/artifact limits, not independent proof of failure**.
- Responses lengthen from about 174 tokens at step 1 to 373 at step 283, but clipping appears in only **5/280 steps**, each at exactly **1/128 responses**, and aborted-response ratio is zero throughout. Widespread truncation or rollout abortion therefore does not explain the regression.
- Most steps have nonzero gradients; final recorded entropy is about 0.561, and there is no numerical collapse. Rollout/training probability correlation remains about 0.9995 and the recorded probability discrepancy/KL is small, so stale or severely inconsistent rollouts are unsupported. Zero PPO KL/clipping is consistent with one PPO epoch, while zero-KL regularization, entropy coefficient, learning rate, and four-GPU execution are not independently shown to be causal.

**Causal chain:** all-tests binary training rewards erase partial progress and make many eight-sample GRPO groups reward-homogeneous; timeout-discarded results can worsen that sparsity and cause long stalls; learning signal remains weak and non-improving despite active updates; frozen held-out exact accuracy consequently never exceeds baseline and finishes below it.

# RL Training Run Diagnosis — `slime_search_r1` (Qwen2.5-3B, Search-R1 recipe)

## Verdict: UNHEALTHY

The run completed and its held-out metric rose (0.048 → 0.165), but it is a failed
agentic-RL run. The policy **extinguished tool use entirely** by step ~50 and then
spent the remaining 65% of the step budget on a flat held-out plateau at closed-book
recall level. Rising training reward over a flat held-out curve is the signature of a
policy exploiting a degenerate reward, not of learning to retrieve.

---

## Root cause (one, concrete)

**The reward function silently discards all format / structure / retrieval shaping and
degenerates to pure binary exact-match. That makes "emit a bare `<answer>` immediately
and never search" a full-reward strategy, and GRPO optimizes straight into it.**

The `--custom-rm-path` is `generate_with_search.reward_func`, which calls:

```python
# examples/search-r1/generate_with_search.py
compute_score_em(
    solution_str=sample.prompt + sample.response,
    ground_truth=sample.label["ground_truth"],
    format_score=SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["format_score"],   # 0.2
)
```

But `compute_score_em` **declares `format_score` and never reads it**. AST inspection of
`examples/search-r1/qa_em_format.py` gives:

```
params: ['solution_str','ground_truth','method','structure_format_score',
         'final_format_score','retrieval_score','format_score','score']
UNUSED params: ['method', 'format_score']
```

The body only consumes `structure_format_score`, `final_format_score`, `retrieval_score`
and `score` — none of which the caller passes, so all three shaping terms stay at their
default **0**. The inline comments in the function body (`# 1`, `# 0.8`, `# 0.3`,
`# 0.2`, `# 0.1`) document an intended non-zero ladder, which confirms the
caller/callee kwarg mismatch is unintended rather than a deliberate design.

Executing the real function against the real prompt reproduces the collapsed reward:

| trajectory | reward |
|---|---|
| correct + valid `<think>`/`<search>`/`<information>`/`<answer>` | 1.0 |
| correct + **bare `<answer>`, no think, no search** | **1.0** |
| wrong + valid format, retrieval block *contained* the gold answer | **0** |
| wrong + bare answer | 0 |

So `reward ≡ 1{EM correct}`. Retrieval earns nothing when the guess is wrong, and costs
nothing to omit when the guess is right. `is_valid_sequence` demands the strict ladder
starting with `<think>`, so a bare answer *is* format-invalid — but the
correct-answer/invalid-format branch returns `score - structure_format_score = 1.0 - 0`,
i.e. **no penalty at all**.

## Causal chain

1. **No reward gradient favors searching.** With `--advantage-estimator grpo`,
   `--n-samples-per-prompt 8` and group normalization
   (`slime/ray/rollout.py::_post_process_rewards`: subtract group mean, `/ (std + 1e-6)`),
   the only within-group discriminator is EM correctness.
2. **Retrieval is pure cost.** `--rollout-max-response-len 1024` caps each turn, and at
   step 0 `rollout/truncated = 0.406` — 40% of trajectories were cut off. A truncated
   trajectory never closes `</answer>`, so `extract_solution` returns `None` → reward 0,
   and it is still trained on (TRUNCATED is only logged, never filtered). Searching was
   systematically zeroed; short answers were not.
3. **Nothing resists the resulting gradient.** `--entropy-coef 0.00`,
   `--kl-loss-coef 0.001`, and the reward-side KL is hard-zero because `--kl-coef` was
   never passed (`slime/backends/megatron_utils/loss.py`: `if args.kl_coef == 0 ...: kl = zeros`).
4. **The policy races to the shortest reward-eligible output** — a bare `<answer>X</answer>`
   then stop — which is exactly what every downstream metric shows.

## Symptoms (consequences, not causes)

- `rollout/response_lengths`: 1751 → ~10 by step 50, then flat 9–12 for 140 more steps.
  Held-out `eval/nq_test/response_len/mean`: 1568.6 → 9.76.
- **Proof retrieval is extinct, not merely terse:** with the Qwen2.5-3B tokenizer, one
  `<search>` turn costs **≥46 tokens** (`<search>…</search>` + `<information>` + the three
  `Doc N(Title: …)` lines `_passages2string` emits at `topk=3`) plus the `<answer>`; a bare
  `<answer>Paris</answer>` is **7**. The observed *mean* of ~10 tokens (train steps 50–190,
  eval step 199 = 9.76) is below the floor for a single search turn — and because it is the
  mean, essentially no sample contains any `<information>` block.
- `rollout/truncated`: 0.406 → 0.000. This reads as an improvement but is a consequence:
  nothing is long enough to reach the 1024 cap anymore.
- `rollout/rollout_log_probs` mean: −1.126 → −0.335. The policy is becoming
  near-deterministic on a 10-token output (confidence/entropy collapse).
- **Held-out plateau:** `eval/nq_test` 0.048 → 0.165 by step ~69, then flat — slope
  **+0.0092 per 100 steps** over steps 69–199 versus **+0.168** over steps 0–59; sd 0.0057;
  range 0.148–0.166 across 14 evals. ~0.165 is closed-book recall for a 3B model and far
  below the ~0.4 NQ-test EM Search-R1 reports for genuinely retrieval-augmented runs.
- **Train/held-out divergence:** `rollout/raw_reward` first-10 mean 0.051 → last-10 mean
  0.206 (max 0.336) while held-out was flat.

## Ruled out — looks anomalous, is not causal

Guarding against misattribution, each of these was checked and cleared:

- **`rollout/rewards` ≈ 1e-9 and `rollout/advantages` ≈ 1e-9 are NOT a dead learning
  signal.** GRPO group-centering makes the *mean* advantage exactly zero by construction;
  `raw_reward` is the un-centered mean and it moves. The policy demonstrably updated
  (response length, logprobs and eval all changed), so advantages were non-zero per-sample.
- **`rollout/kl` = 0.0 exactly is by design**, not a broken KL: `--kl-coef` was never
  passed, so `loss.py` zeroes that tensor. KL still enters through `--use-kl-loss`
  (coef 0.001) — simply far too weakly to counteract the collapse.
- **`extract_solution`'s `if len(matches) <= 1: return None` is correct, not a bug.** The
  dataset prompt itself contains one `<answer> Beijing </answer>` demonstration (verified in
  `nq_hotpotqa_train/test.parquet`), so a model answer yields exactly 2 matches and
  `matches[-1]` is the model's answer; `<= 1` correctly detects "no answer produced".
- **The stop-tag edit in `generate_with_search.py` is not the root cause.** `no_stop_trim=True`
  is confirmed at `slime/rollout/sglang_rollout.py:103`, so `</search>`/`</answer>` are
  retained, tags stay balanced, and `execute_predictions` still parses `<search>` and loops up
  to `max_turns=8` — multi-turn retrieval remains fully possible. Its effect is to make a clean
  single-turn `<answer>` terminate reliably, which *sharpens* the reward for the shortcut
  rather than creating it. Secondary amplifier at most.
- **`--num-rollout 3000` (effective args) vs `--num-rollout 200` (`run_qwen2.5_3B.sh`) is not
  causal.** `outputs/metrics.json` documents the snapshot as frozen at train step 200 / eval
  step 199 of a longer job, and the collapse is already complete by step ~50.
- **The truncated log (200 of 3000 steps) is not itself a defect.** It is the documented
  historical cutoff, and every claim above is established well inside that window.

## Distillation

Root cause: reward-shaping collapse — `format_score` is passed to a parameter
`compute_score_em` never reads, so all structure/retrieval credit terms default to 0 and
reward reduces to binary EM with **no penalty for skipping retrieval**.

Symptoms: 10-token response floor below the 46-token cost of one search turn, zero
truncation, logprob rise to −0.335, held-out plateau at 0.165 with slope +0.009/100 steps,
and rising train reward against flat held-out reward.
